subject: Infra capacity & unit economics - QBR prep: data, owners, and slides
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Infra capacity & unit economics - QBR prep: data ask

Team,

As we prep for the June QBR (leadership review on 2027-06-14) I need a tight set of slides and numbers focused on: GPU spend YTD, effective unit cost per served token (post-batching & caching), cluster utilization by pool/model, and a sensitivity analysis for +/-20% traffic.

Concrete asks (deliver by EOD 2027-06-07):
- Laura: consolidated GPU spend by pool (month-to-date and YTD) + per-pool utilization heatmap. Attach: capacity_model_template.xlsx
- Rishi: unit-cost calculation: show raw token cost, effective token cost after batching/caching, and a simple normalized "tokens per $1" metric. + one slide of risk/assumptions.
- Diego: run the prefix-caching experiment numbers (top 20 prompts) and produce delta to token volume and latency. Share any runbooks if enabling cache affects SLOs.
- Monica: customer impact notes: list of big customers (2-3) who require SLA guarantees and if dedicated capacity needs to be proposed.
- Markus: capacity ask: recommended committed/reserved headroom (absolute GPUs) and an ops playbook for sudden +30% spikes.

Attachments: capacity_model_template.xlsx (attached)

Keep slide drafts to 1-2 bullets each — we'll consolidate into the leadership pack. If anything is unsure about the metric definitions, call me.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Infra capacity & unit economics - QBR prep: data ask

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear asks. I attached a short PDF (cost_breakdown_Q2.pdf) with preliminary spend and utilization snapshots. Highlights:
- GPU spend YTD (hosted + dedicated): $5.2M; Q2 to date $1.6M.
- Utilization (week of 2027-05-24): pooled inference clusters avg 68% util, tail at 93% during peak hours (17:00-19:00 PT).
- Model breakdown: large LLMs (70B+) account for ~42% of tokens but 58% of GPU time due to longer sequences and higher batch fragmentation.

Open questions: what granularity do you want for the sensitivity analysis? Hourly? Daily? For capacity asks, we typically show headroom required to keep 99th p95 latency within SLO at +20% traffic; confirm if that is the leadership ask.

Attached: cost_breakdown_Q2.pdf (summary) and a CSV export in the drive link.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Infra Finance & Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-04T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Infra capacity & unit economics - QBR prep: data ask

+1 on Laura's note. A couple of modeling points I want included in the slides:
- Unit-cost definition: please show both "raw GPU token cost" (GPU spend / raw tokens served) and "effective token cost" (GPU spend / effective tokens after batching + prefix caching). For the QBR, leadership likes a simple "tokens per $1" metric, e.g., 480k tokens/$1 baseline -> 560k tokens/$1 with batching improvements.
- Sensitivity: run the model for -20%, baseline, +20%, +40% to show non-linear effects due to queuing and batch-size drop.
- Latency tradeoffs: include the quantified tail-latency change for enabling larger batching windows (we have experimental numbers; Diego can confirm).

Draft slide suggestions (one-sentence bullets):
1) Spend & utilization: YTD spend and current shortfall vs target run-rate.
2) Unit economics: baseline vs with caching/batching and tokens-per-$1 change.
3) Capacity ask: recommended reserved GPUs and cost delta.
4) Risks & mitigations: SLO/regression lanes and canary plan.

I can draft the unit-cost slide if you want; will need the per-model throughput numbers (p50/p95 token/sec) and the batching distribution.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Economics
Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-06T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Infra capacity & unit economics - QBR prep: data ask

Fwd: experimental run results + model update (see attachment capacity-model-v2.xlsx and drive link)

On Tue, 2027-06-06 at 09:10, Diego Fernandez wrote:
> Team —
> I ran the prefix-caching experiment across the top 20 prompts for a week (staging traffic shadow). Early topline: prefix caching reduced total served tokens by ~12% for the sample, with median p95 token latency unchanged and p99 improving by ~6%.
>
> Key numbers (sample week):
> - Token volume delta: -12.1%
> - Effective GPU time delta: -9.8% (some overhead for cache lookup ops)
> - Per-request tail latency (p99): improved by 6% on average for cached flows; non-cached flows unchanged.
>
> I updated the capacity model (attached). If we enable prefix caching for the top 20 prompts in prod, projected annualized savings ~ $420k, with an ops rollout risk that needs a short runbook (cache warm-up, cache size limits).
>
> Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcDEFcapacitydoc
> Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/ENGINF-1428 (rollout + runbook)
>
> Attachment: capacity-model-v2.xlsx (delta tab populated).
>
> -Diego

Diego Fernandez
SRE Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Infra capacity & unit economics - QBR prep: data ask — summary & owners

Thanks all — good progress. Quick summary and owners so we can lock slides tomorrow (2027-06-08) for consolidation: 

Decisions/next steps:
- Unit-cost slide: Rishi will draft the unit economics slide (tokens/$1 baseline vs with batching/caching). Rishi to pull per-model throughput by EOD 2027-06-07 (received partial numbers; will finalize).
- Spend & utilization: Laura to finalize GPU spend tables and the pool utilization heatmap (use the CSV in the drive).
- Caching experiment: Diego's results look promising; proceed to draft rollout runbook in ENGINF-1428. Diego to include a 3-step canary (shadow -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%).
- Capacity ask: Markus to propose reserved headroom (expressed as number of A100-equivalent GPUs) and the cost delta slide. Show both committed and on-demand options.
- Customer impact: Monica to list top-3 customers with SLA needs and recommend which ones should be offered Dedicated capacity as part of QBR follow-up.

Slides to produce (owners):
1) Spend & Utilization (Laura)
2) Unit Economics & Sensitivity (Rishi)
3) Capacity Ask & Options (Markus)
4) Caching Experiment & Runbook (Diego)
5) Customer Impact & Recommended Actions (Monica)

Deadline: Please upload final slides to the Drive folder (link below) by 2027-06-08 18:00 PT. I will do a 30-minute dry-run with the slide owners on 2027-06-09 at 10:00 PT.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcDEFcapacitydoc
Jira: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/ENGINF-1428

If anyone needs more runtime numbers (per-model batching distribution, p95/p99 token/sec) ping Diego directly. Good work so far — keep the decks tight.

Vivek
